name: Gulf / US–Iran war
value: Hormuz shut; tankers hit mines 11 Nov
summary: Iran says Hormuz stays shut until its demands are met; IRGC says three tankers hit mines; US blockade continues
state: Iran's Mohsen Rezaei denied talks with the US and said Hormuz stays shut until Tehran's seven conditions, including lifting the US naval blockade, are met; the IRGC said three tankers caught fire after hitting mines in the eastern strait, reported 11 Nov (Al Jazeera). UKMTO reported incidents involving two tankers, and monitors count at least 37 attacks on ships in and near the strait in November. US officials said on 9–10 Nov new strikes on Iran were unnecessary (CBS News). The closed strait and shipping attacks set the Alert.
for_you: Mariners should follow UKMTO and Joint Maritime Information Centre guidance. Travellers to the Gulf should check FCDO travel advice. A closed Hormuz tends to keep oil, gas and shipping costs elevated.
rubric_hit: Alert: Strait of Hormuz substantially closed; attacks on shipping (37+ in Nov)

sources.title: Al Jazeera — Iran denies talks with US, says Hormuz will stay shut until demands are met
CBS News — Iran downplays new U.S. task force aimed at disrupting ground transport routes

why: Direct hostilities between Iran and the US or Israel threaten Gulf energy infrastructure, the Strait of Hormuz and the wider region.
drivers: Strikes and retaliation, attacks on shipping and Gulf states, mediation and ceasefire talks, US force posture.

rubric.alert: Active strikes between states, attacks on Gulf energy infrastructure or shipping, or the Strait of Hormuz substantially closed.
rubric.watch: A ceasefire or stalemate with sporadic strikes, or credible threats of renewed strikes.
rubric.normal: No direct state-on-state hostilities; diplomacy active.
